rv.q: The play lumbers somewhat in the last third when the conclusion has already been telegraphed, but under Britt Berke's sure-footed direction, Phyl exhibits the dramatic craft and social conscience of other works of the era by George Bernard Shaw, John Galsworthy, and Harley Granville-Barker. It’s also a fun time, and a worthy revival.

Phyl (Lily Ganser, Stereophonic , in an impressive Off Broadway debut) is a spirited young governess in charge of two nasty children, Betty (Tessa Bilmes) and Olive (Charlotte Van Ledtje), daughters of the wealthy, imperious, straitlaced Mrs. Ponsonby (Katie Firth). Act One transpires in the schoolroom of her grand home.
Some of the period costumes delivered by Alicia J. Austin could be better tailored and finished.
This is an entertaining play with meat on it and an utterly captivating production.

cn.t: Critics praise Mint Theater's spirited revival of Hamilton's 1913 feminist dramedy, with Lily Ganser's compelling performance elevating a historically intriguing but occasionally creaky rediscovery about a governess defying social constraints.
